summary: This document describes the URN Namespace Identifier "ddi" for resources that conform to specifications from the Data Documentation Initiative Alliance. The Alliance is not affiliated with the IETF or ISOC. This is an Independent Submission, not a standard, and does not have IETF community consensus.

eli5.summary: Names for things can start with a short word. This reserves "ddi" for naming research data documents so they can be found.

subtitle: A persistent naming scheme for research data documents.

tldr.problem: Research data needs persistent, globally unique identifiers that are independent of any one organization or storage location, so that different systems can reliably reference the same data resources across time and different repositories.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9517 registers a new URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace called "ddi" for the Data Documentation Initiative, a metadata standard used by research organizations. Resources get identifiers like urn:ddi:us.agency:resource-id:version, which are resolved through DNS records to find which services can access them.
tldr.outcome: Research institutions and data archives can now use persistent, standardized identifiers for their data, supporting discovery and interoperability across distributed systems without requiring a single central registry.

today: RFC 9517 was published in January 2024 as an Informational document from an Independent Submission. It is not an Internet Standard. The URN namespace "ddi" has been registered with IANA, and the DDI Alliance operates the infrastructure for managing and resolving these identifiers. Data documentation initiatives and research organizations can now use DDI URNs to create persistent identifiers for their resources.

sections.title: What is DDI and why does it need a URN namespace?
sections.content:
The Data Documentation Initiative (DDI) Alliance is an international group that creates standards for documenting and managing research data. These standards help researchers describe every stage of data work: from planning a study, through collecting and processing data, to sharing and archiving it. DDI specifications are used by universities, government agencies, and data centers worldwide.

Because research data is often used across many organizations and stored in multiple repositories, the data needs a reliable way to be identified and located no matter where it is stored or who is using it. This RFC registers a new URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace called "ddi", which is a persistent naming standard that does not depend on any single location, company, or website remaining online. Unlike URLs, which point to a specific web address, URNs are permanent names that can be resolved to find current locations.
sections.eli5: When you move, your phone number stays the same because it's registered with the phone company. This RFC lets research data have the same kind of permanent name that doesn't change when it's stored in a different place.

sections.title: The DDI URN structure and how it works
sections.content:
A DDI URN has three parts separated by colons: urn:ddi:agency:resource:version. The agency identifier works like a reversed domain name (for example, us.ddia1 for an agency in the US), the resource identifier uniquely names a specific data item within that agency, and the version identifier distinguishes different versions of the same resource.

For example: urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:AggregationMethod:1.0 refers to version 1.0 of a controlled vocabulary (a list of allowed values) for aggregation methods. The DDI Alliance maintains a registry of agency identifiers and ensures they are unique. Individual agencies then manage the resource identifiers within their own namespace, much like domain names work on the web.
sections.eli5: It's like an address: the country, the town, the street, and the house number. Each part tells you more specifically where to find what you're looking for.

sections.title: Resolving DDI URNs through DNS
sections.content:
When a system needs to find a resource with a DDI URN, it does not look it up in a central database. Instead, it uses the DNS (Domain Name System, which normally translates web addresses like google.com). The DDI URN agency identifier is converted into a DNS name, and DNS servers delegate the request to the appropriate agency's servers. Those servers then respond with information about available services—such as a repository where the actual data can be retrieved, a registry describing the data, or a URL where more information is available.

This decentralized approach means no single organization controls all DDI URN resolution. Each DDI agency operates its own DNS servers and decides what services it offers. The DDI Alliance provides central coordination by operating the root delegation for the "ddi" namespace in DNS.
sections.eli5: Instead of asking one big library desk, you ask a local library desk in your town. That desk knows which books are in your local library and directs you to find them.

sections.title: Security and management
sections.content:
DDI URN identifiers are names for public, research data that anyone can look up, so there are no high security requirements for basic DDI URN resolution. However, the DDI Alliance must ensure that agency registrations are legitimate and that DNS records are protected against tampering. The RFC notes that the quality of DNS security depends on the security of DNS itself; organizations can improve this by using DNS over HTTPS (DoH) to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks on DNS queries.

An agency that controls a DDI namespace is responsible for the persistence and accessibility of its data. If an agency shuts down or stops maintaining its servers, the data may become unreachable, even though the URN itself remains a valid permanent name.
sections.eli5: The system trusts that agencies keep their contact information accurate in DNS, just like the post office trusts that people keep their mailing addresses correct.
